title: A first look at the submillimeter Sun with ALMA
question: What are the disk structures, center-to-limb brightness temperature variations, and chromospheric electron temperature profiles of the quiet Sun in the first full-disk ALMA Band 7 (0.86 mm; 347 GHz) solar images, combined with Bands 3 and 6?

data.bands: Band 3 (3 mm; 100 GHz), Band 6 (1.26 mm; 239 GHz), Band 7 (0.86 mm; 347 GHz)

what.value: ALMA commissioning observations from December 2015 used in Papers I and II

evidence.quote: The results are shown in the top panel of Fig. 3, where we have included, for comparison, data from the commissioning observations of December 2015, which were also used in Papers I and II.

what.value: Recommended quiet Sun central disk brightness temperatures for ALMA Bands 3 and 6

evidence.quote: together with the percentage differences from the quiet Sun central disk brightness temperatures recommended by (cite: 2017SoPh..292...88W) (in bold)

what.value: Disk center brightness temperatures and atmospheric parameters from Paper II

evidence.quote: The derived brightness temperatures of the center of the disk are given in Table 1, together with the recommended values and those of Paper II
together with the recommended values and those of Paper II, for the four spectral windows of each ALMA band and for the average frequency

recipe.goal: Acquire, select, and map full-disk Total Power images
recipe.method: Process 12-m TP double-circle scan observations using JAO CASA scripts and the methodology of White et al. (2017), selecting antennas with better T_sys (PM03 for Band 3, PM04 for Band 6, PM02 for Band 7) and applying CASA sdgaincal before mapping to suppress arc-like brightness modulations in Band 7.
key_parameters: Band 7 beam FWHM = 21 arcsec; scan duration = 3 min
assumptions: Arc-like modulations are associated with opacity variations and can be corrected by adjusting gains relative to the central field position in double-circle scans

recipe.goal: Compare full-disk and central-region solar structures across wavelengths
recipe.method: Compare ALMA Band 7 full-disk and central 500'' x 500'' images against AIA 1700 Å, 1600 Å, and 304 Å images and GONG H-alpha (and negative H-alpha) images smoothed to the ALMA resolution.
key_parameters: Central region size = 500'' by 500''; smoothed to 21'' ALMA resolution

recipe.goal: Extract, correct, and frequency-remap center-to-limb brightness temperature variations
recipe.method: Measure T_b(mu) across the disk in Bands 3, 6, and 7, apply diffuse light correction as in Paper I, exclude limb regions within 70'', 35'', and 30'' in Bands 3, 6, and 7 respectively, and remap all measurements to a common reference frequency f_ref = 100 GHz via mu_100 = (f/f_ref)^2 * mu.
assumptions: Both free-free and H^- absorption coefficients are proportional to f^-2

recipe.goal: Cross-normalize datasets and fit combined CLV curve to derive disk-center brightness temperatures
recipe.method: Normalize Band 6 and Band 7 datasets (and current Band 3 dataset) relative to December 2015 Band 3 commissioning data (normalization factor fixed to 1) via a simultaneous least-squares fit of all sets to a third-degree polynomial in ln(mu): T_b(mu) = A_0 + A_1 ln(mu) + A_2 ln^2(mu) + A_3 ln^3(mu). Evaluate disk center T_b for Bands 3, 5, 6, and 7.
key_parameters: Band 3 commissioning normalization factor = 1; polynomial degree = 3
assumptions: Absolute calibration of the December 2015 Band 3 commissioning observations is accurate

recipe.goal: Invert radiative transfer equation to derive electron temperature profile T_e(tau_100)
recipe.method: Analytically invert the radiative transfer formal solution for a third-degree polynomial in ln(tau), T_e(tau) = a_0 + a_1 ln(tau) + a_2 ln^2(tau) + a_3 ln^3(tau), using Euler constant and Riemann zeta integrals to obtain coefficients a_0, a_1, a_2, a_3 from A_0, A_1, A_2, A_3, and compare with FAL93 models A, C, and F.
assumptions: Thermal bremsstrahlung and H^- emission in local thermodynamic equilibrium; plane-parallel formal solution of radiative transfer equation

score_reason: The ALMA project code, observing dates/times, antenna selections, radial cutoffs, and analytical inversion equations are all explicitly given, and the main results are numeric tables. However, the diffuse light correction details are deferred to Paper I, the exact December 2015 commissioning dataset code is not stated, and the fitted normalization factors and CASA/sdgaincal parameters are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA Total Power data (2019.1.01532.S) with a clear mathematical recipe for CLV frequency remapping, polynomial fitting, and analytical radiative transfer inversion yielding specific numeric disk-center brightness temperatures and atmospheric parameters.
